newsitem.title: USA: SmithKline says trials show Kytril effective.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says trials show Kytril effective.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham said Tuesday results of two trials showed the company's anti-emetic Kytril tablets are as effective as an intraveneous drug in preventing nausea in some chemotherapy patients.
The company said the trials compared the effectiveness of Kytril and ondansetron, an intravenous medication for prevention of nausea and vomiting.
The company said Kytril is the first anti-nausea tablet for use with high-dose cisplatin, a chemotherapy with the highest potential of causing nausea and vomiting.
It said the results of the two studies were presented this week at the 33rd annual meeting of the American Society of Clinical Oncology in Denver.
